solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Oblique creative work written about poetry

indicators.note: 'about' can mean turned round, so the word is written the other way

blocks.note: art is creative work
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A critic calls a slanted, indirect piece of art that comments on poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: As an adjective, TRAVERSE is an old word for lying or running across, the sense the clue uses.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare adjective describes something lying crosswise or at a slant, matching a slanting, sideways direction.

clue.text: Time the BBC cut back on no-good provocations?

definitions.note: the answer is a gerund used as a mass noun, standing for the plural

indicators.note: cutting something at the back trims off its final letter

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Critics wonder whether it is time the BBC stopped airing worthless provocative content.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie (or Auntie Beeb) is the affectionate British name for the BBC; lose its last letter and put NG on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunting is the act of jeering at someone to provoke them, so it sums up a series of provocations.

clue.text: Cereal Croat reinvented can cause gas

indicators.note: something reinvented is remade in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Croatian's new breakfast cereal recipe turns out to cause flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' looks like wind after a bowl of cereal, but in American English the gas is the pedal you press to speed up.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the gas pedal is the car's accelerator, so stepping on the gas means pressing it.

clue.text: Staying fresh and vital or always off-colour?

blocks.note: ever means always
someone off-colour or nauseous looks green

explanation.surface: A question of whether someone is perennially youthful or permanently queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Off-colour is British for slightly unwell, and a sickly person is said to look green.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen describes something that never loses its freshness or appeal, like a plant keeping its leaves all year.

clue.text: Alluring female trying to get a Jack on the rocks?

definitions.text: trying to get a Jack on the rocks

blocks.note: first meaning: a seductive, dangerously attractive woman

blocks.clueFragment: trying to get a Jack on the rocks
blocks.note: second meaning: the mythical singer who lured sailors onto rocks; a jack (Jack tar) is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seductive woman at a bar hoping someone will buy her a Jack Daniel's with ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack on the rocks' reads as whiskey over ice, but Jack is a sailor and the rocks are where the Sirens of Greek myth wrecked ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sirens of Greek legend sang so beautifully that passing sailors steered toward them and were wrecked.

clue.text: Axe discovered in Incan cellar

indicators.note: something discovered inside other words is found sitting within them

blocks.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: An archaeologist unearths an ancient axe in the storeroom of an Inca dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axe' looks like a tool found on the dig; it is a verb meaning to scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe a project or programme is to scrap it or call it off, a common journalistic verb.

clue.text: A large amount of ale can ruin especially stodgy starters

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so the opening letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Drinking lots of beer can spoil a meal, particularly heavy first courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' looks like the first course of a meal; here it means the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech, acres of something means a great quantity, as in acres of space or acres of print.

clue.text: My middle is devoid of muscle ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is taken
being devoid of something means lacking it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: the core is the middle of something
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone laments that their midriff has lost all its muscle tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive, but it is the exclamation of surprise. Cor is a British exclamation, as in 'Cor blimey!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal exclamations of surprise or admiration, so 'My!' and 'Cor!' are interchangeable interjections.

clue.text: I’m surprised after bishop knocked out sailor

indicators.note: something knocked out is removed from where it stood

blocks.note: Blimey! is a British exclamation of surprise
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Astonishment that a sailor managed to floor a bishop in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'I'm surprised' stands for the exclamation BLIMEY, from which B goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Limey is old American slang for a British sailor, from the lime juice given against scurvy in the Royal Navy.

clue.text: This chap manages to choke foremost of cats!

definitions.text: This chap manages to choke foremost of cats

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its front, so only the first letter is kept
choking means gripping round the throat, so one piece closes around another

blocks.note: he refers to a man
to rule is to manage or govern
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a hero who strangles the greatest of all cats.
explanation.walkthrough: The C sits inside RULES just after its R. Read whole, the clue recalls the first of the hero's labours, strangling the Nemean lion.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the strongman killed the Nemean lion, the mightiest of cats, by choking it with his bare hands.

clue.text: Relative with a touch of rheumatism is not easy to see

indicators.note: a touch is just a small trace, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: an uncle is a relative
taken as written
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An elderly relative with mild joint pain whose condition is hard to diagnose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not easy to see' reads like a symptom; it is the definition, meaning indistinct.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclear is blurred or obscure, hard to make out with the eyes or the mind.

clue.text: Vibrator heard rumbling for a while

indicators.note: something seen only for a while is a short stretch of a longer run, a part of the whole phrase

blocks.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a sex toy buzzing audibly for some time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vibrator' points at something racier; it simply means a thing that vibrates.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin membrane in the ear shakes in response to sound waves, passing them on to the inner ear.

clue.text: Genteel criminal I see coming across well on TV

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters I and C, said in turn, make the phrase, a standing crossword convention

explanation.surface: A refined crook who notices he looks good on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' poses as a noun beside 'Genteel', but it is the anagram signal; IC for 'I see' is a letter sound crosswords use.
explanation.definitionFit: Telegenic people have looks and manner that appear attractive and appealing when filmed for television.

clue.text: Extremely stylish topless woman out of The Sun?

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so the outer letters are kept
having no top means losing the first letter

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A very fashionable topless model who does not appear in The Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid long known for topless models on Page 3; here it is just the sun, and being out of it means in shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A shady spot is sheltered from direct sunlight, so anything there is out of the sun's rays.

clue.text: Where some go to get high in trailer Ma converted

definitions.text: Where some go to get high

indicators.note: something converted is changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother's caravan turned into a place where people take drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get high' suggests drugs in a trailer; it means getting up into the sky on a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers go to an airport building to board planes that climb to cruising altitude.

clue.text: Tend to swear after getting caught out by knight

indicators.note: out means removed, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for knight
to curse is to swear
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A batsman who tends to swear after being caught out by a fielder named Knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Caught out is a cricket dismissal; here C (caught) is removed from CURSE, and N for knight goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a patient is to look after them, the same as tending to someone who is ill.

clue.text: Squid Game essentially must stop racial casting

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the middle letters are kept
casting can mean shaping or throwing about, so the letters are reformed
a stopper plugs a gap, so one piece is pushed inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
the two middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A demand that the TV hit Squid Game end its racially biased choice of actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squid Game' reads as the Korean drama title; split it, and 'Squid' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is the Italian-derived name for squid, especially when served as food in battered rings.

clue.text: The King’s fit to be taken for trustworthy

blocks.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, King Charles; the 's is read as 'is'
food fit to be eaten is edible

explanation.surface: The King is in good enough shape to be considered reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'The King's' is short for 'is'. 'Fit to be taken' first suggests fitness; here it is food fit to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone credible can be believed, so they are worth trusting and relying on.

clue.text: Film a spinster for Spooner in parade of cars

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously mixed up the opening sounds of words, so initial sounds are exchanged

blocks.note: a film is a thin coat, and a spinster is an old maid; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: A director wants to shoot an unmarried woman in a procession of vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' is a verb on the surface but a noun meaning a thin layer here. The swap only works in a British accent where 'coater' and 'motor' drop their R.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcade is a formal procession of cars, usually escorting a dignitary through the streets.

clue.text: Schubert composed in a remote place, according to an Aussie

definitions.text: a remote place, according to an Aussie

indicators.note: to compose is to arrange elements into a work, so the letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Australian claims Schubert wrote music in some isolated spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' is the natural verb for a composer, which hides its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians call remote, sparsely settled country covered in brushwood the scrub, far from towns.

clue.text: Sweet comment about Slormgorm seems sincere… initially

indicators.note: 'about' can mean turned around, so the word runs backwards
initially means at the start, so first letters are taken

blocks.note: a note is a brief comment
the setter refers to himself, so ME
first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A kind remark about the setter Slormgorm appears genuine, at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as kind, applying to the comment; it is the definition, a dessert. A setter's own pseudonym usually stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton mess is a British dessert of crushed meringue, strawberries and cream, traditionally served at Eton College.

clue.text: Offensive husband collaring European canines?

indicators.note: a collar goes around a neck, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: the Tet Offensive was a 1968 Vietnam War campaign
H is the abbreviation for husband
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A rude husband grabbing hold of some European dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like an adjective meaning rude; it is a noun, the Tet Offensive. 'Canines' suggests dogs, but means pointed teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Canines are the pointed teeth beside the incisors, so they are examples of the wider category.

clue.text: Display indifference if horse wears small wig

indicators.note: something worn goes on the body, so one piece is covered by another

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
rug is slang for a wig or toupee

explanation.surface: Someone not caring if a horse puts on a tiny wig.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is drug slang for heroin, which crosswords shorten to H.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising and dropping the shoulders is a gesture showing a lack of concern or interest.

clue.text: Wise men first appearing in stable by donkeys

indicators.note: what appears first is the opening letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: first letter of the word
donkey's years is British slang for a very long time, ages

explanation.surface: The Magi turning up at the Nativity stable beside the donkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Donkeys' looks like the animals in the stable; it is short for donkey's years, meaning ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A sage is a person revered for profound wisdom, so wise men are sages.

clue.text: Board or fare

blocks.note: first meaning: to climb aboard a bus or train
second meaning: to manage or progress, as in 'how are you faring?'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' and 'fare' suggest a bus ticket, but fare here is a verb meaning to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both climbing onto a vehicle and making progress or coping in life.

clue.text: Dope provided by Maori with snug pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are rubbishy and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drugs supplied by a New Zealander wearing tight trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' first suggests drugs; it means a fool. 'Pants' looks like trousers, but in British slang it means rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, and an ignoramus is someone ignorant or uneducated.

clue.text: Regularly need to have Bud as a state

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: taking alternate letters of the word, the first and third, gives these two
bud is American slang for a friend or pal

explanation.surface: Someone who routinely needs a Budweiser to get into a certain condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bud' looks like a beer, and 'a state' like a drunken condition; one is a friend, the other a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a sovereign country in the Himalayas, and state can mean a nation.

clue.text: General one left to surround old army of privates

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose on all sides, so one pair goes around another

blocks.note: Gen is the abbreviation for General
the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for left
the Territorial Army, Britain's former volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A general with a lone soldier flanking a veteran army of rank-and-file soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privates' reads as low-ranking soldiers, but means private parts. The TA was renamed the Army Reserve in 2014, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Genital means relating to the sexual organs, which are euphemistically called one's privates.

clue.text: Fresh at the moment (making love close to fridge)

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the final letter is kept
making one thing into another means changing it, so one letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: now means at the moment
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like O
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cheeky aside about someone being amorous right now beside the fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as 'making love into close to fridge': the O for love turns into E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fresh has only just been made or arrived, so it is recent and unused.

clue.text: Architect heading to LA to open unopened bridge?

indicators.note: a heading is what goes at the top, so the first letter is taken
not opened means losing the front, so the first letter goes
opening something up lets another piece be put inside it

blocks.note: first letter
a bridge spans a gap, so it is cryptically a spanner

explanation.surface: An architect travels to Los Angeles to inaugurate a bridge that has not yet opened.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful idea that a bridge is something that spans, a spanner. L goes inside the shortened word, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect designs and plans buildings, and the word also means the mastermind behind a scheme.

clue.text: Broadcasting company’s finally in the red

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so the last letter is taken

blocks.note: final letter of the word
to be in the red is to be in debt, owing money

explanation.surface: A media company ends up losing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting' suggests TV and radio, but its original meaning is scattering seed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting originally meant scattering seed widely over a field, which is a way of sowing.

clue.text: Oh Boy! bags large hit for US vocal group

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside a sack, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: Gee! is an American exclamation like 'Oh boy!'
L is the abbreviation for large
to club is to hit

explanation.surface: Delight that a boy band has scored a big hit with an American singing group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' reads as a chart success; it is the verb, to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee club is a choir, especially at an American school or college, singing short part-songs.
